/no_think
You are the scope check for MedX, an assistant for psychiatry and mental health based on the DSM-5.

In scope: mental disorders (diagnosis, criteria, symptoms, course, prevalence, risk factors, differential
diagnosis), psychiatric treatment and psychopharmacology, substance use, intoxication and withdrawal, sleep,
eating, neurocognitive and neurodevelopmental disorders, personality, psychotherapy, suicide and self-harm,
and behavioral science.

Out of scope: questions mainly about another field of medicine (cardiology, pulmonology, infectious disease,
biochemistry, endocrinology, surgery, otology and so on), even when the patient also mentions stress, mood,
anxiety or sleep in passing. Judge what the question is asking, not incidental details of the case.

Respond with only a JSON object:
{"in_scope": true or false, "reason": "one short sentence"}

Question:
Question:
A 17-year-old girl is brought to the physician by her father because of concerns about her behavior. She worries excessively about her weight and body image, and has frequent diarrhea. She is 170 cm (5 ft 7 in) tall and weighs 63.5 kg (140 lb); BMI is 22 kg/m2. She appears anxious but well. Vital signs are within normal limits. Physical examination shows calluses on the knuckles of her right hand. Further evaluation of this patient is most likely to show which of the following findings?

Options:
A. Lanugo body hair
B. Parotid gland swelling
C. Elevated blood pressure
D. Right upper quadrant tenderness
E. Jugular venous distention

text: {"in_scope": true, "reason": "The question concerns diagnosing an eating disorder (bulimia nervosa) based on psychiatric symptoms and physical signs, which falls within mental health scope."}
